doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: Musicians as healers
summary: Monk and she talk about the glow of elder musicians, and she describes them as healers and the work as a sacred task.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: I sort of know what you mean. I’ve been in company with some of these people like Milt Hinton and there’s something about their glow, they’re like magnets.
People want to stand next to them because they make you feel better.

Well it’s their vibration that they –the frequency that they vibrate from. You know? They said, I can’t remember if it was Leonard Cohen or Bob Dylan said that the music is up there and we just bring it down. You know? Musicians bring it down. And I do believe that with all my heart. You know? They are healers. You know? The musicians are the healers of the world and I can’t imagine getting through life, and I always used to say that to our audience, you know they were there when you fell in love and they were there when you got divorced. The music is what got us through life. So it ended up becoming a very beautiful – it wasn’t a job, it was a way of life. It was like a sacred task to usher and transition these people at a time in life at an age where they had been forgotten, the phone didn’t ring, they couldn’t do three hour, three sets anymore. There was incapacitation. No one had money or insurance for doctors you know. Once you’re of Medicare age, you know, it’s generally too late. You can have advanced stages of cancer. Don’t forget there was smoking for years in the clubs. You know all sorts of things that affected their health you know. Sorry, that’s another creditor.
